Jasmin: Heads up — noticed a latency regression on llama-3-13b-chat after yesterday's kernel-selector change. 8-12% p50 increase on chat workloads with long system prompts. :eyes:
Rui: Oof. I wired up perf profile from canary — looks like additional GEMM time in attention and more memory churn during KV restores. Posting snippet.
Rui: ```
# top hotspots (canary, 1x A100)
AttentionGEMM            42.1ms  +9.8ms
KVRestore                18.5ms  +7.3ms
RMSNorm                  6.9ms   +1.2ms
SiLU_fwd                 3.0ms   +0.6ms
Total token cost         79.5ms  +11.8ms
```
Alex: Thanks — two quick things to check: 1) kernel selection fallback is preferring a non-fused matmul for head_dim=64 on that build, 2) chat template is pre-pending ~120 tokens default system prompt so KV-cache entries are bigger than before.
Michael: Re: head_dim — we saw earlier that head_dim alignment (64 vs 80) interacts with cuBLAS heuristics. If kernel chooser picks generic path, GEMM lanes blow up. Suggest adding head_dim->preferred_kernel mapping in selector.
Sara: Also, rope_theta scaling: with the template length increase, our RoPE default (rope_theta=10000) shifts phase more quickly and makes some fallback attention code path do extra rotary unrolls. Might be contributing to KVRestore time.
Rui: Here's the exact profiler stack for KV restore:
Rui: ```
KVRestore
  memcpy_device_to_device  5.2ms
  unpack_kv_shards         9.6ms
  allocate_tmp_buffers    2.7ms
  attention_reindex       0.9ms
```
Alex: Good breakdown. allocate_tmp_buffers spikes when we switch kernel implementations because buffer shapes differ. That explains extra allocs. We can unify buffer shape or reuse a preallocated slab.
Michael: For RMSNorm vs SiLU — the candidate fused kernel for RMSNorm+SiLU used by the new runtime shows a small correctness tweak; fallback to scalar path for some models. Might be a micro regression but accumulates. We should gate the fused kernel behind a regression test.
Sara: Proposed short-term mitigations:
- revert the kernel-selector change for Llama-3-13b chat routes (canary)
- add a head_dim->kernel override for common dims (64, 80, 128)
- preallocate KV slab sized for longest chat template we support
- add perf test that runs long-system-prompt chat scenario in CI
Jasmin: Agreed. I also want to tune rope_theta defaults per hidden size. My suggestion: map by hidden_size -> rope_theta multiplier so we don't use global 10000 for all. e.g. hidden_size 512 -> 6000, 1024 -> 9000, 2048+ -> 10000. Thoughts?
Michael: That mapping seems reasonable. Need to run numeric checks (phase wrap, precision). I'll run a small sweep.
Rui: I'll prepare a targeted microbench to compare:
- kernel selector old vs new
- with/without slab prealloc for KV
- rope_theta mapping on/off
Alex: Command to reproduce locally (docker):
Alex: ```bash
docker run --gpus all -it --rm redwood/infer-test:canary \
  ./bench_chat --model llama-3-13b --template long_sys.json --nbatches 100 --profile=trace.out
```
Sara: Also: batching heuristic note — current auto-batcher increases batch window to hit throughput targets; with long prefixes that causes larger per-request KV sizes and higher variance. For chat routes we should cap the batch window when prefix_len > 64. Simple throttle.
Jasmin: OK owners: Rui = perf microbench & trace; Alex = revert canary + kernel-override PR; Michael = rope_theta sweep & fused-kernel gate; Sara = batching cap + KV slab prealloc prototype. I'll open tickets and link here. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated for service=llama-3-13b-chat at 1779123490 by alex — reason: perf regression observed.
Alex: Rollback in progress. I'll also post the PR with kernel-override and tests.
Rui: I'll upload the full traces and attach to the ticket. Expect initial numbers in ~2 hours.
Jasmin: Thanks everyone. If you find any model-specific oddities (mixtral/mistral/qwen) flag here — we want to avoid one-off fixes. Closing loop after microbench results. :white_check_mark:
